extracted.intended_audience: patent and trademark attorneys, applicants, Turkish Patent and Trademark Office staff, and IP practitioners in Turkey
extracted.subtask_short: turkish patent and trademark office regulations
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes statutory duties, procedural requirements, personnel rules, attorney qualifications, disciplinary standards, and appeal procedures set out in amendments to the Law on the Establishment and Functions of the Turkish Patent and Trademark Office (Law no. 5000 and related provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Geographical Signs duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Geographical Signs shall conduct the recording, search, examination, assessment and registration processes related to geographical signs and traditional product names; perform the announcement and registry processes of geographical signs and traditional product names; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Re-examination and Evaluation — scope and appeal timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Re-examination and Evaluation shall conduct the processes of examining and evaluating the appeals against the final decisions given by the relevant department on the proceedings about the industrial property rights and traditional product names, which would be made within two months of notification of the said decision by persons being party to those proceedings and whose interests would be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals to this Department must be made within two months of notification of the relevant department's final decision; the Department examines/evaluates those appeals directly under the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Re-examination and Evaluation — Board composition for decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on the subject requested to be examined and evaluated shall be taken by a Board comprised under the chairmanship of the Head of Department with the participation of at least two expert members specialized in the field to be examined and evaluated and who had no connection to the decision of the Office being appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board must include impartial expert members (at least two) without ties to the underlying decision; chaired by Head of Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-examination decisions — finality and judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisions of the Department of Re-examination and Evaluation shall be final. A legal proceeding can be instituted against these decisions at Ankara Intellectual and Industrial Rights Civil Court within two months of the notification date of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Department decisions are final administratively, affected parties may bring judicial proceedings at the specified Ankara court within two months of notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of execution for annulment-related verdicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Until finalized, the verdict related to the annulment of the decisions of the Board of Re-examination and Evaluation may not be executed. This provision shall also apply for verdict annexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execution of annulment-related verdicts is suspended until the verdict is finalized; prescription periods commence with the date of the final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Support Services duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Support Services shall perform renting and purchasing activities in the framework of the Public Financial Management and Control Law no. 5018; perform or procure cleaning, security, lighting, heating, repair, transport and similar services; arrange and execute central registry and archive activities; conduct processes related to the movable and immovable properties of the Office as per relevant legislation; plan and execute civil defence and mobilization services; execute library services; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Information Technology duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Information Technology shall monitor information technologies and determine the automation strategies of the Office, take the precautions necessitated by information security, generate solutions conforming to public information technology standards; conduct the information technology services of the Office; perform technical studies related to web pages, electronic signature and electronic document applications; collect information related to the services of the Office and create databases; conduct works related to the establishment, maintenance, supply, development and updating of the existing information technology infrastructure of the Office and ensure communication security; ensure data transfer among the Office and the documentation centres and the national and international organizations that the Office cooperates with; collect information from domestic and foreign sources related to industrial property in electronic media, evaluate and submit such information to related units; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Strategy Development duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Strategy Development shall perform the tasks assigned to strategy development and financial services unit as per Law no. 5018, Article 15 of Law no. 5436 and other legislation; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Counsel duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal Counsel shall perform the tasks assigned to legal units as per the provisions of Decree Law no. 659 related to the Execution of Legal Services at Public Administrations covered by the General Budget and Private Budget Administrations; perform other works as assigned by the Presidency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Board member appointment qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of the Office’s Management Board shall be appointed among persons that have graduated from a domestic or abroad higher education institution of at least four years duration, with sufficient occupational knowledge and ten years of experience. Representatives of the Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Finance shall have at least ten years of employment in the relevant Ministry and adequate occupational knowledge and experience; one member to be determined by the Minister of Science, Industry and Technology shall be a representative of the Turkish Union of Chambers and Stock Exchanges with at least ten years of experience. These members should also bear the conditions at paragraph (a) of Article 48 of the Civil Servants Law no. 657.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment of domestic and foreign experts — terms and wage cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic and foreign experts may be employed under a contract for a provisional term domestically or from abroad based on the approval of the Management Board. The net amount of wage to be paid to these experts shall be determined by the Management Board such that this wage does not exceed the monthly average net salary paid to a first degree Industrial Property Expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure and rules related to their employment shall be determined with a regulation to be enforced with the decision of the Council of Ministers based on the Office suggestion and Minister proposal. For specific expertise, a work contract may be made by Management Board resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may utilize external organizations and fee handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may utilize the services of domestic and foreign organizations in the execution of processes related to industrial property rights. The fees for such services shall be collected by the Office together with the fees of the services to be given by the Office and payments to the relevant organizations shall be made by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized representatives before the Office (who may act for applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: As regards industrial property rights and traditional product names, the natural persons or legal entities with authority to provide consultancy and perform on behalf of the applicants operations before the Office shall be: the patent attorneys for patent, utility model and integrated circuit topography topics; the trademark attorneys for trademarks, geographical signs and traditional product names; and both patent attorneys and trademark attorneys for designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions to become a patent attorney or trademark attorney (natural persons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural persons shall satisfy the following conditions to become a patent attorney or trademark attorney: (a) Being a citizen of the Republic of Turkey; (b) Having capacity to act; (c) Having graduated from a higher education institution providing at least four years of undergraduate education or equivalent abroad; (d) Not having been sentenced for specified intentional crimes (including certain serious crimes listed) even if pardoned and even if periods in Article 53 of the Turkish Criminal Code have expired; (e) Having domicile in Turkey; (f) Having successfully passed patent attorney or trademark attorney examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The law lists specific disqualifying offences (e.g., crimes against State security, embezzlement, bribery, fraud, laundering, smuggling) — conviction for these bars admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal entity attorney requirements and representation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A legal entity patent or trademark attorney must be founded as a limited liability or incorporated company under Turkish law; the operation subject must cover the activity of patent attorney or trademark attorney and be represented by a natural person attorney. Even if a natural person attorney is partner or employee of multiple legal entity attorneys, he may use attorney authority to represent only one legal entity attorney; persons using authority in that manner may not act as a natural person attorney. The natural person attorney shall be jointly and severally responsible together with the represented legal entity attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent/trademark attorney examinations, registration and insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent attorney and trademark attorney examinations are held once every two years by resolution of the Management Board. Only persons satisfying statutory conditions shall be admitted. It is obligatory for successful candidates to be registered in the Patent Attorneys Registry or Trademark Attorneys Registry to act. The period and amount of occupational liability insurance for initial registration and renewals shall be determined by the Management Board. The procedure and rules related to examination and registry processes, certificate issuance, registration renewal and related matters shall be determined by regulation. Examination and registration fees shall be determined by the Office. For matters not covered, provisions of the Turkish Code of Obligations no. 6098 related to power of attorney shall apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary penalties — types and triggering actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary penalties enforceable on patent and trademark attorneys include: (a) Warning — written notification to act more attentively when violating occupational codes; (b) Reprimand — written notification that person is flawed in execution, applied to those who received warning and repeat within two years or fail obligations or act for parties with conflicting interests; (c) Temporary retention from attorneyship activity — prohibition of attorney activity for not less than three months and not more than one year, applied to those who received reprimand and repeat within five years, or who misuse attorney powers or Office identifiers to cause confusion; (d) Banning of attorneyship — prohibition for indefinite period, applied to those who received temporary retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists progressive penalty steps and examples of misconduct triggering each level (repeated misconduct, conflicts of interest, misuse of title/domain/Office promotional means).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary procedure and temporal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority to give disciplinary penalty lapses if investigation is not launched within three months after having been informed of the commitment of such actions, and in any case the disciplinary penalty is not enforced within two years of commitment. It is obligatory to give the penalties listed within 30 days of conclusion of the investigation. Disciplinary penalties may not be given without acquiring the defensive statement of the attorney; the attorney is deemed to withdraw defense if the defensive statement is not submitted within the duration prescribed by the investigator (not less than seven days). Disciplinary penalties take effect on the date decided and are enforced immediately. Administrative justice may be applied against decisions; persons banned as a result of a finalized disciplinary decision may not become attorneys again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary Board composition, appointment and membership rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Board of Patent and Trademark Attorneys is comprised of seven persons: one member from the Ministry, three members from the Office, and three members among patent or trademark attorneys who have not been penalized with any of the specified penalties; substitute members equal in quantity and quality are determined. All members are appointed by the Minister of Science, Industry and Technology. Before the President suggests attorney members, he shall obtain the opinion of two chambers of commerce with the highest number of members and two attorneyship associations with the highest number of members. Tenure is three years. If a legal proceeding has been instituted against a member for specified crimes, that member may not attend meetings until the end of the proceeding and a substitute attends instead. Members who fail to attend two consecutive meetings without excuse or who lose eligibility shall have membership dropped and substitute members take their place. Other procedures and rules will be regulated by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff reclassification and titles update
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel working as patent examiner and trademark examiner at the Office on the effective date of this Law shall be deemed as assigned to the industrial property examiner position; assistant patent and assistant trademark examiners shall be deemed assigned to the assistant industrial property examiner position, with their present staff degrees, without the need to take any action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annexes to Civil Service staff lists are amended accordingly; titles in various laws and annex lists are updated from 'Institute' to 'Office' and examiner titles are harmonized to 'Industrial Property Examiner'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation indemnity for reassigned personnel (provisional article)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the total net amount of the contract wage of the last month related to the former staff position of personnel deemed assigned to counselor staff exceeds the total net amount of the contract wage of the new staff position, the difference shall be paid as a separate indemnity without being subjected to tax or deduction until the difference is closed. This indemnity payment shall cease for persons whose staff title changed by their request or who were assigned to other institutions at their own request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The indemnity covers differences in net wage and related supplements (excluding overtime and certain fees); applies until equalized, subject to cessation conditions described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative renaming and reference harmonization
rubrics_metrics.description: All references in other legislation to 'Turkish Patent Institute' shall be deemed references to 'Turkish Patent and Trademark Office'; 'Trademark Examiner' and 'Patent Examiner' shall be deemed referred to as 'Industrial Property Examiner', and related terminology in multiple laws and annex lists are amended accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a blanket harmonization of terminology across statutes (Law no. 5000, related IP laws, public finance lists, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annulment of specified older Decree-Laws and provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Decree-Law No. 551 (Protection of Patent Rights), No. 554 (Industrial Designs), No. 555 (Geographical Indications), No. 556 (Trademarks) and No. 566 (amending Decree-Law No. 551) are annulled. Specific sub-paragraphs of Law no. 5000 and other law provisions are revoked as listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The legislation explicitly lists which older decree-laws and statutory provisions are annulled as part of the reform.
